newsitem.title: DENMARK: Mobil signs first Neds gas sale contract.
newsitem.headline: Mobil signs first Neds gas sale contract.

text.p: COPENHAGEN, June 11, Reuter - Mobil Corp's Mobil Europe Gas Inc (MEGAS) has signed its first contract to sell natural gas from its production in the Netherlands, to an end user in Germany, President and General Manager of MEGAS Dr Axel Commichau told Reuters on Wednesday.
"We have signed a contract. It will be for a sizeable proportion of our Dutch production, done at arms length terms and conditions," said Commichau.
He added that the gas will be sold by Mobil's Dutch subsidiary to the German Mobil system for "optimisation, modulation and upgrading," before being sold on to the end user.
But in effect, he added, it was a direct sale. "Only now are we legally entitled to bring gas directly into the German system".
MEGAS broke new ground last month by becoming the first company to announce it had sold gas directly to an end user in the Netherlands from its U.K. production.
The gas will be sent through the Interconnector pipe, which will link Bacton in the U.K. to Zeebrugge in Belgium and will open in October 1998.
Commichau saw growing integration as a key trend in the developing European market.
"Moscow is now more or less connected with Lisbon, Norway with Rome, the Dutch to a large network. The UK is the last big producer but it is now also hooked up," he said.
Growing liberalisation, in which governments are taking a lead, was also critical.

"First came the British, the Germans will be next, the Dutch made a surprise move by publishing a White Paper a year ago, and Brussels is trying to hammer down a gas liberalisation drective," he said.
MEGAS is trying to take advantage of these trends by coordinating subsidiaries in several European countries.
Mobil produces gas in the U.K., Germany, the Netherlands, Norway and Austria. It is also exploring in Denmark, Hungary and Italy.
"We are a European player," he said, "We are no longer five national players but a European player where we can clearly see these trends impacting on our business".
It was the recognition that the market was becoming freer and more integrated that led Mobil to set up MEGAS, he said.

Having created the company as a kind of "umbrella body" to coordinate the activities of affiliates, he said it was a logical decision to sell surplus UK gas to the Netherlands and surplus Dutch gas to Germany.

"I can't rule out any more Interconnector deals in the future. We are open," he said. "We had a lot of success in the 17th round (of UK North Sea licensing) and we are very positive about our exploration possibilities. We may have a surplus soon."
Mobil's current European production is around 14 billion cubic metres (bcm) a year, Commichau said, and sales are around 15 bcm a year.
He said that Mobil was not driving the European gas market, describing instead MEGAS' strategy as a "fast follower approach."
